name: Timely Filing PTF.2 — Provider Timely Filing (Proof of Timely Filing — PX_TF Bypass & Pay) Navigator
description: Walk the Provider Timely Filing SOP for a late claim that is nonetheless payable on Acceptable Proof: review the Timely filing pop-up criteria and Exclusion indicator, compare State and CFT and determine the 90-day rule applies, walk the Non-ITS Home / corrected-claim / Sutter / participation gates, find the prior deleted claim is outside the TFL, confirm Acceptable Proof (PWK) has been received and approved, then apply the PX_TF bypass code and submit Pay.

steps.name: Identify the PX_PTF hard edit on Event Resolution
steps.description: Open the Event Resolution tab. All edits on the claim are listed; the PX_PTF edit (PX_590 — 'Claim submit time limit exceeded') is the active hard edit, flagged in red. That is the event you are resolving.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab.
steps.hint: Click the 'Event Resolution' tab. The active PX_PTF edit (PX_590 — 'Claim submit time limit exceeded') is shown in red as the Hard Edit you must resolve.
steps.checklistItem: Event Resolution tab opened — PX_PTF hard edit identified

steps.name: Open the Provider Information tab
steps.description: Review the timely filing limit for the claim by opening the claim and scrolling to the Provider Information tab. The timely filing reference is located in the Billing section.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Provider Information tab.
steps.hint: Open the 'Provider Info' tab and scroll to the Billing section — the Timely Filing Limit field is here.

steps.name: Open the Timely filing pop-up
steps.description: Navigate to the Provider Information tab, then the Billing section, and click the question mark (?) icon next to the Timely Filing Limit field label. The Timely Filing pop-up window will open, with the provider's Tax ID and State fields automatically populated.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks the '?' icon, which dispatches the open_tf_popup action.
steps.hint: Click the '?' icon next to 'Timely Filing Limit' in the Billing section — the Timely filing pop-up opens with the Tax ID and State auto-populated.

steps.name: Look up TFL criteria and Exclusion indicator
steps.description: In the Timely filing pop-up, click the Search button. A row of filing criteria will appear with the fields State, CFT, Contract/LOB, Par, Effective, End date, and TFL. Note the values: State CA, CFT 52, Contract/LOB Commercial, Effective, End date, and TFL 365. Then interpret the Exclusion indicator: if Exclusion ind = No, the provider is not excluded from the 90-day rule and must submit the claim within 90 days from the date of service; if Exclusion ind = Yes, the provider is excluded and a custom timely filing limit may apply, but only if every field in the pop-up matches the corresponding value on the claim. In this scenario, the Exclusion indicator is Yes, so each field must be compared against the claim before applying the custom limit.Also compare the State displayed in the Timely Filing pop-up with the Pricing State by navigating to the Provider Information tab, then the Rendering section. Confirm that the values match. In this scenario, both fields display CA, indicating that the State requirement has been satisfied.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks Search inside the Timely filing pop-up, which dispatches the tf_search action and reveals the filing-criteria rows.
steps.hint: In the Timely filing pop-up, click 'Search'. The filing-criteria rows appear — note State CA, CFT 52, Contract/LOB Commercial, TFL 365, and read the Exclusion ind. Here Exclusion ind = Yes, so every field must match the claim before the custom TFL applies.
steps.checklistItem: Look up TFL criteria and Exclusion indicator

steps.name: Compare CFT against claim type
steps.description: Compare the CFT (Claim File Type) field from the pop-up against the claim type displayed in the Details sub-tab of the Claim Data tab — 52 for a professional claim and 53 for an outpatient claim. In this scenario, the claim type is Professional, so the CFT value is 52. The Contract/LOB field is treated as Commercial in this scenario, so no further check is required for that field.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Details sub-tab inside Claim Data to read the claim type (CFT 52 for Professional).
steps.hint: Open 'Claim Data' → 'Details'. Claim type is Professional → CFT 52, which matches the pop-up. Contract/LOB is Commercial, so no further check.

steps.name: Determine the applicable filing limit
steps.description: Note the Receipt date from the claim summary, along with the Billed, Allowed, Paid, and Action code values. Then confirm whether the Receipt date falls within the Effective and End date range shown in the Timely Filing pop-up window (Navigate to the Provider Information tab, then the Billing section, and click the question mark (?) icon next to the Timely Filing Limit field label.). Apply the result: if Exclusion ind (Provider info tab) = Yes and every field matches, the provider must submit the claim within the TFL shown in the pop-up's TFL field; if Exclusion ind = Yes but any field does not match, the 90-day rule applies; if Exclusion ind = No, the 90-day rule applies. In this scenario, the Receipt date does not fall within the Effective and End date range shown in the pop-up, so the provider must follow the 90-day rule.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee returns to the Provider Information tab to weigh the claim summary Receipt date against the pop-up's Effective/End range. The date comparison is on trust (the engine has no date primitive).
steps.hint: Read the claim summary Receipt date and compare it to the pop-up's Effective–End range. It falls outside the range — so the 90-day rule applies.

steps.name: Verify the claim is Non-ITS Home
steps.description: Determine whether the claim is ITS Home by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Details sub-tab, and reviewing the Additional Claim Data section. If the claim is identified as ITS Home, follow the alternate SOP steps. If the claim is identified as Non-ITS Home, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the claim type is Professional, which is classified as Non-ITS Home; therefore, the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee returns to Claim Data → Details to confirm the claim is Non-ITS Home.
steps.hint: On Claim Data → Details, the ITS Home field reads No — the claim is Non-ITS Home, so proceed.
steps.checklistItem: Verify the claim is Non-ITS Home

steps.name: Check for the PX_PAJ event
steps.description: Determine whether the claim contains a corrected claim event by looking for the PX_PAJ event in the Event Resolution tab. In this scenario, the PX_PAJ event is present, so the next condition (the Frequency value) must also be checked before concluding whether the claim is a corrected claim.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab to look for the PX_PAJ event.
steps.hint: Open 'Event Resolution' and look in the All Edits section — the PX_PAJ event is present. Check the Claim Header's Frequency next.

steps.name: Confirm the Frequency value
steps.description: Confirm the Frequency value by navigating to the Claim Header tab, then the General Claim Data section. A claim is considered a corrected claim when a PX_PAJ event is present and the Frequency field is set to 7. When both conditions are met, the alternate SOP for corrected claims must be followed. If either condition is not met, the claim is not considered a corrected claim, and the trainee may proceed with the next step.In this scenario, the Frequency value is not 7. Therefore, the claim is not a corrected claim, and the trainee may proceed with the next step.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Header tab to confirm the Frequency value.
steps.hint: Open 'Claim Header' and check the Frequency field under General Claim Data. It is not 7 — so even with the PX_PAJ event this is not a corrected claim, and the trainee proceeds.

steps.name: Check for the PX_SUT event
steps.description: Determine whether the provider is Sutter by looking for the PX_SUT event in the Event Resolution tab. If the PX_SUT event is present, follow the Sutter procedure; if it is absent, the provider is not Sutter and the trainee proceeds. In this scenario, the PX_SUT event is absent, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab again to look for the PX_SUT event.
steps.hint: Open 'Event Resolution' again and scan the All Edits section for a PX_SUT event — there is none, so the provider is not Sutter and the trainee proceeds.

steps.name: Verify provider participation status
steps.description: Verify the claim type and provider status by navigating to the Claim Header tab, then the General Claim Data section, and reviewing the Provider Participation field. The claim type has already been confirmed as Professional. To proceed, the Provider Participation field must display PAR, indicating that the provider is participating. If the claim type is Professional and the provider status is PAR, proceed to the next step. Otherwise, follow the alternate SOP steps. In this scenario, the claim type is Professional and the provider status is PAR; therefore, the trainee may proceed to the next step.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Claim Header tab again to verify the Provider participation field.
steps.hint: Open 'Claim Header' again and check the Provider participation field under General Claim Data. It reads PAR — the claim is Professional and the provider is Participating, so proceed.

steps.name: Look up prior deleted claims
steps.description: Review the member's claim history to check whether the same claim was previously deleted because it was submitted with incorrect data or because the provider data was not loaded at the time. Navigate to the Search tab → Claims sub-tab — the Service from date, HCID, and Provider Tax ID are auto-populated. Enter the Service to date and click Search. Two matching claims are listed — one active claim with status Pending-Investigation and one with status Resolved-Cancelled. Open the Resolved-Cancelled claim's member information; if the Finalization code field shows PX_RDELEP, the claim was previously deleted.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks Search on the Search → Claims sub-tab, which dispatches the claims_search action and reveals the two matching claims.
steps.hint: Open 'Search' → 'Claims', enter the Service to date, and click 'Search'. Two claims appear — open the Resolved-Cancelled claim's member information; the Finalization code PX_RDELEP shows it was previously deleted.

steps.name: Verify the deleted claim's filing window
steps.description: Search tab → Claims sub-tab → View member information → Open claim detail. To check whether the deleted claim was within the TFL. The deleted claim's details appear in the same layout as the current claim. Note the Service from date of the claim line and the Receipt date and calculate the difference. If the difference is within 90 days, the deleted claim was within the TFL. If a deleted claim is found and is within the TFL, follow the alternate SOP steps; if there is no deleted claim or it is outside the TFL, proceed with rejection. In this scenario, the deleted claim was filed outside the TFL, so the trainee proceeds to the Acceptable Proof check.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee clicks 'Open claim detail' on the Resolved-Cancelled claim, which dispatches the open_prior_claim action. The 90-day calculation is on trust (the engine has no date primitive).
steps.hint: Click 'View member information' on the Resolved-Cancelled claim, then 'Open claim detail' in the dialog. The gap between its claim line's Service from date and Receipt date exceeds 90 days — the deleted claim was outside the TFL, so the trainee proceeds to the Acceptable Proof check.
steps.checklistItem: Verify the deleted claim's filing window

steps.name: Check for Acceptable Proof in PWK section
steps.description: Check whether Acceptable Proof has been received to override the TFL. Navigate to the Attachments tab → Attachments sub-tab and review the PWK section. If a proof document has been submitted, the Type and Document number fields will be populated. If proof has been received and approved, apply the PX_TF bypass code and continue processing; if no proof has been received or it has not been approved, proceed to reject the claim. In this scenario, proof has been received and approved, so the trainee proceeds to apply the PX_TF bypass code.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Attachments sub-tab on the Attachment tab to review the PWK section.
steps.hint: Open 'Attachment' → 'Attachments' and review the PWK section. The Type and Document number fields are populated — Acceptable Proof was received and approved, so proceed to apply the PX_TF bypass.
steps.checklistItem: Check for Acceptable Proof in PWK section

steps.name: Apply the PX_TF bypass code and validate
steps.description: In the Bypass Codes section of the Event Resolution tab, select PX_TF in the Bypass code field and click the Validate button in the claim summary to apply the bypass.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes only when the trainee clicks the claim summary Validate button while the selected bypass code is 'PX_TF' (PX_TF — Timely filing bypass). Any other code does not complete the step.
steps.hint: Open 'Event Resolution' → Bypass Codes, select 'PX_TF — Timely filing bypass', then click the claim summary 'Validate' button.
steps.checklistItem: Apply the PX_TF bypass code and validate

steps.name: Submit Pay decision
steps.description: Navigate to the Decision section in the header, select 'Pay' from the dropdown menu and click Submit.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee confirms the Pay decision in the submit dialog.
steps.hint: Pick 'Pay' from the Decision dropdown in the claim header, then click Submit and confirm in the dialog.

stepSummaryForResults.name: Event Resolution tab opened — PX_PTF hard edit identified
Frequency not 7 — not a corrected claim
PX_SUT event absent — provider is not Sutter
Deleted claim confirmed outside the TFL
Acceptable Proof received in PWK section
PX_TF bypass code applied and validated
